nodes.summary: In the dining philosophers transition system with atomic acquisition of both forks, for each philosopher $i \in \{0, 1, 2\}$, from every state reachable from the initial state (all three philosophers thinking) a state in which philosopher $i$ eats is reachable, in zero or more steps.
nodes.title: Under atomic acquisition every philosopher can always still eat

nodes.summary: In the dining philosophers transition system with atomic acquisition of both forks, every state reachable from the initial state (all three philosophers thinking) has a successor: some philosopher can move.
nodes.title: Atomic acquisition prevents deadlock

nodes.summary: The labelled transition system on the states of the three philosophers, labelled by the philosopher that moves: there is a step labelled $i$ from $s$ to $t$ exactly when either philosopher $i$ thinks in $s$, neither of its forks $i$ and $i + 1$ (modulo $3$) is held in $s$, and $t$ is $s$ with philosopher $i$ eating; or philosopher $i$ eats in $s$ and $t$ is $s$ with philosopher $i$ thinking. A fork is held as in…
nodes.title: Dining philosophers with atomic fork acquisition

nodes.summary: In the dining philosophers transition system with atomic acquisition of both forks, for each philosopher $i \in \{0, 1, 2\}$, in no state reachable from the initial state (all three philosophers thinking) do philosopher $i$ and its neighbour $i + 1$ (modulo $3$) both eat.
nodes.title: Mutual exclusion under atomic acquisition

nodes.summary: In the dining philosophers transition system of the naive protocol under a butler, for each philosopher $i \in \{0, 1, 2\}$, from every state reachable from the initial state (all three philosophers thinking) a state in which philosopher $i$ eats is reachable, in zero or more steps.
nodes.title: Under a butler every philosopher can always still eat

nodes.summary: In the dining philosophers transition system of the naive protocol under a butler, every state reachable from the initial state (all three philosophers thinking) has a successor: some philosopher can move.
nodes.title: A butler prevents deadlock

nodes.summary: The labelled transition system on the states of the three philosophers, labelled by the philosopher that moves: there is a step labelled $i$ from $s$ to $t$ exactly when philosopher $i$ can move in $s$ under the naive protocol, if philosopher $i$ is thinking then fewer than two philosophers hold a fork in $s$, and $t$ is $s$ with philosopher $i$ advanced one phase (thinking to holding its first fork, to eating, to…
nodes.title: Dining philosophers with a butler

nodes.summary: In the dining philosophers transition system of the naive protocol under a butler, for each philosopher $i \in \{0, 1, 2\}$, in no state reachable from the initial state (all three philosophers thinking) do philosopher $i$ and its neighbour $i + 1$ (modulo $3$) both eat.
nodes.title: Mutual exclusion under a butler

nodes.summary: Philosopher $i$ can move in state $s$ when it thinks and neither of its forks $i$ and $i + 1$ (modulo $3$) is held in $s$, or when it eats (it then puts both forks down); a philosopher holding only its first fork cannot move. A fork is held as in the naive protocol: philosopher $j$ holds fork $j$ when it holds its first fork or eats, and holds fork $j + 1$ when it eats.
nodes.title: Enabled moves under atomic acquisition

nodes.summary: Philosopher $i$ can move in state $s$ when it can move in $s$ under the naive protocol and, if it is thinking, fewer than two philosophers hold at least one fork in $s$. Under the naive protocol each philosopher $i$ picks up the left fork $i$ first and then the right fork $i + 1$ (modulo $3$), each only when no philosopher holds it, and an eating philosopher can always put both forks down.
nodes.title: Enabled moves under a butler

nodes.summary: Given a protocol and a state, philosopher $i$ can move exactly when it is thinking (phase $0$) and its first fork is not held by any philosopher, or it holds its first fork (phase $1$) and its second fork is not held by any philosopher, or it is eating (phase $2$), in which case its move puts both forks down.
nodes.title: When a philosopher can move

nodes.summary: The CTL formula $\neg\,\mathsf{EX}\,\top$ over the philosophers as atoms. It holds at a state exactly when the state has no successor; in the transition system of a protocol, exactly when no philosopher can move.
nodes.title: The deadlock formula

nodes.summary: The valuation of the atoms $i \in \{0, 1, 2\}$ on the states of the dining philosophers: atom $i$ holds at a state exactly when philosopher $i$ is eating there, that is, when its phase is $2$.
nodes.title: The eating valuation

nodes.summary: Given a protocol and a state, fork $f$ is held exactly when some philosopher $i$ either has $f$ as its first fork and is in phase $1$ or $2$, or has $f$ as its second fork and is in phase $2$ (eating).
nodes.title: Held forks

nodes.summary: The state in which all three philosophers are thinking, that is, every phase is $0$.
nodes.title: Initial state of the dining philosophers

nodes.summary: For a protocol $P$, the labelled transition system on the states whose labels are the philosophers: there is a transition from $s$ to $t$ labelled $i$ exactly when philosopher $i$ can move in $s$ under $P$ and $t$ is the state obtained from $s$ by the move of philosopher $i$.
nodes.title: Transition system of a dining-philosophers protocol

nodes.summary: In a state $s$ (the phases of the three philosophers), the move of philosopher $i$ changes only the phase of $i$: if $i$ is thinking, it starts eating, picking up both forks at once; otherwise it goes back to thinking. The phases of the other two philosophers are unchanged.
nodes.title: Move of a philosopher under atomic acquisition

nodes.summary: The state obtained from $s$ when philosopher $i$ moves: the phase of $i$ advances from thinking ($0$) to holding its first fork ($1$), from $1$ to eating ($2$), and from eating back to thinking; the phases of the other philosophers are unchanged. Whether the move is allowed is not checked here.
nodes.title: Move of a philosopher

nodes.summary: Consider the transition system of the naive protocol, in which every philosopher $i$ picks up fork $i$ first and fork $i + 1$ second (indices modulo $3$), with atom $i$ read as "philosopher $i$ is eating". Its initial state, where all philosophers are thinking, satisfies the CTL formula $\mathsf{EF}$ applied to the deadlock formula: from it, a state in which no philosopher can move is reachable.
nodes.title: The naive protocol can deadlock

nodes.summary: In the transition system of the naive protocol, with atom $i$ read as "philosopher $i$ is eating", the state in which every philosopher holds its first fork (every phase is $1$) satisfies the deadlock formula: no philosopher can move there.
nodes.title: A deadlock state of the naive protocol

nodes.summary: For every philosopher $i$, in the transition system of the naive protocol, with atom $j$ read as "philosopher $j$ is eating", the initial state satisfies $\mathsf{AG}$ applied to the formula that philosophers $i$ and $i + 1$ (indices modulo $3$) do not both eat: in no state reachable from the initial state, where all philosophers are thinking, are philosophers $i$ and $i + 1$ both eating.
nodes.title: Mutual exclusion under the naive protocol

nodes.summary: The protocol in which every philosopher $i \in \{0, 1, 2\}$ picks up fork $i$ (its left fork) first and fork $i + 1$ (modulo $3$) second.
nodes.title: Naive dining-philosophers protocol

nodes.summary: For a philosopher $i \in \{0, 1, 2\}$, the CTL formula $\neg(p_i \wedge p_{i+1})$ over the atoms $p_0, p_1, p_2$ (one per philosopher), with indices modulo $3$. Under the valuation in which $p_j$ holds when philosopher $j$ eats, it says that the neighbouring philosophers $i$ and $i + 1$ do not eat at the same time.
nodes.title: Neighbours-apart formula

nodes.summary: In the transition system of the three dining philosophers under the resource-ordered protocol, with the atom $p_j$ holding when philosopher $j$ eats, the initial state, in which everybody thinks, satisfies the CTL formula $\mathrm{AG}\,\mathrm{EF}\,p_i$ for every philosopher $i \in \{0, 1, 2\}$: from every state reachable from the initial state, some state in which philosopher $i$ eats is reachable.
nodes.title: Every philosopher can still eat under resource ordering

nodes.summary: In the transition system of the three dining philosophers under the resource-ordered protocol, the initial state, in which everybody thinks, satisfies the CTL formula $\mathrm{AG}\,\mathrm{EX}\,\top$: every state reachable from it has a successor, that is, some philosopher can move.
nodes.title: Resource ordering prevents deadlock for the dining philosophers

nodes.summary: In the transition system of the three dining philosophers under the resource-ordered protocol, with the atom $p_j$ holding when philosopher $j$ eats, the initial state, in which everybody thinks, satisfies the CTL formula $\mathrm{AG}\,\neg(p_i \wedge p_{i+1})$ for every philosopher $i \in \{0, 1, 2\}$, with indices modulo $3$: in no state reachable from the initial state do philosophers $i$ and $i + 1$ both eat.
nodes.title: Neighbours never eat together under resource ordering

nodes.summary: The protocol in which every philosopher $i \in \{0, 1, 2\}$ picks up the lower-numbered of its two forks $i$ and $i + 1$ (modulo $3$) first and the higher-numbered one second: philosophers $0$ and $1$ take fork $i$ first, and philosopher $2$ takes fork $0$ first and fork $2$ second.
nodes.title: Resource-ordered dining-philosophers protocol

nodes.summary: For a state $s = (s_0, s_1, s_2)$ of the three dining philosophers and a philosopher $i \in \{0, 1, 2\}$, the phase of philosopher $i$ in $s$ is the component $s_i$.
nodes.title: Phase of a philosopher

nodes.summary: A protocol for three philosophers $i \in \{0, 1, 2\}$ sitting between forks $0, 1, 2$ consists of two maps $\mathrm{first}, \mathrm{second}$ from $\{0, 1, 2\}$ to itself, the fork philosopher $i$ picks up first and the one it picks up second, such that for every $i$ these are its two neighbouring forks $i$ and $i + 1$ (modulo $3$) in some order: either $\mathrm{first}(i) = i$ and $\mathrm{second}(i) = i + 1$, or…
nodes.title: Dining-philosophers protocol

nodes.summary: The number of seated philosophers in a state $s$ is the number of philosophers that hold at least one fork in $s$, that is, whose phase is either holding the first fork or eating.
nodes.title: Number of seated philosophers

nodes.summary: For a state $s = (s_0, s_1, s_2)$ of the three dining philosophers, a philosopher $i \in \{0, 1, 2\}$ and a phase $p \in \{0, 1, 2\}$, setting the phase of philosopher $i$ to $p$ gives the state obtained from $s$ by replacing the component $s_i$ by $p$ and keeping the other two components.
nodes.title: Updating the phase of a philosopher

nodes.summary: A state of the three dining philosophers is a triple $(s_0, s_1, s_2)$ with each $s_i \in \{0, 1, 2\}$ the phase of philosopher $i$: $0$ thinking, $1$ holding the first fork, $2$ eating (holding both forks).
nodes.title: Dining-philosophers state

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
